one_line_contribution: That the harm from an organically accumulated ALFWorld experience bank is carried by episode-specific state facts (object-receptacle placements, open/closed states) that were true in the source episode and are false in the target - not by wrong procedures and not by token volume - established by a deterministic, LLM-judge-free labeling of every retrieved fact against the target task's ground-truth initial state from the game file, and remediated by a read-time typed-placeholder redaction of those facts that is compared at matched k and matched tokens against abstention, utility filtering, provenance gating and reliance steering with clean-task cost charged to each.
closest_prior_work: The Trap of Trajectory (arXiv:2605.09330, VERIFIED via s2cli/Semantic Scholar: 2026-05-10, cit 1) is the sharpest threat and the proposal knows it. It frames agentic-memory failure as reliance on spurious patterns of three types and proposes CAMEL, a write- and retrieval-time calibration that reduces that reliance 'while preserving or improving performance on clean inputs' - which is verbatim the proposal's own headline structure (remove the harm at zero clean-task cost). The proposal's Risk section concedes that if one of CAMEL's three pattern types is instance-specific state, the contribution collapses to the census plus the matched-token content-vs-volume test. That taxonomy has been public since May 2026 and is readable in full; writing a proposal whose novelty turns on an unread paragraph of the nearest neighbour is not a resolved novelty argument, it is a deferred one. Secondary threats, both verified: When Memory Lies (arXiv:2608.04574, s2cli, 2026-08-05) already pairs stale spatial memory claims with a downstream navigation task and finds auditing only partially mitigates - the same failure shape in a VLM/FrozenLake substrate, though with a single planted memory claim rather than an organically accumulated bank, and with detection rather than fact-level redaction as the control; and Honest Lying (arXiv:2605.29463, s2cli/HF, 2026-05-31) runs on ALFWorld and shows agents acting on stored task interpretations that the environment has reset away from, which is the 'wrong' side of the proposal's typology and so sharpens rather than pre-empts the stale-true/wrong split. When Continual Learning Moves to Memory (arXiv:2604.27003, verified, 2026-04-29, cit 3) already establishes that representation choice governs reuse and that finer-grained organization is not universally good; the insights-only-bank ablation here is largely a mechanistic re-derivation of that. Also verified and correctly characterized by the proposal: 2607.10608 (Compliance Trap / E-P-R, 2026-07-12), 2606.05684 (AdaMEM, 2026-06-04), 2605.05583 (Belief Memory, 2026-05-07, cit 5), 2601.03192 (MemRL, 2026-01-06, cit 83), 2608.10509 (MAP-Graph provenance, 2026-08-11, cit 4), 2601.05107 (Controllable Memory Usage / reliance steering, ACL 2026-01-08), 2602.04288 (Contextual Drag), 2605.10828 (First Drop of Ink). No cited ID failed verification.
strongest_objection: The program's own prior result already dissolves the problem the proposed method solves, and the plan never commits to a prediction that would rescue it. The brief states that cutting injection from seven items to three eliminated the harm from the same bank. The proposal's headline is that redaction 'removes the harm at the same k that produced it' - but k=7 is only worth defending if k=7 buys something on clean tasks that k=3 does not, and no prediction (P1-P6) asserts or tests that redacted k=7 beats raw k=3 on clean tasks. raw k=3 appears in the baseline list with no falsification condition attached to it. So the study's most likely outcome is 'redaction works' alongside 'and so did just retrieving less, at zero implementation cost' - a complicated read-time transform for a solved problem, ALFWorld-specific because the redaction regexes exploit observation templates the paper itself admits do not transfer to WebShop or tool use. A second, independent objection: the outcome variable is too sparse for P1. The pilot produced zero fixes and six to seven breaks; even scaled to 600 tasks x 3 seeds, the discordant-pair count is plausibly in the low tens, and a regression of net flip on stale-fact count, token count and four item-type counts on that many events will return a token-count CI containing zero because every CI contains zero. P1 is then confirmed by absence of power rather than by evidence - an unfalsifiable prediction wearing a falsification condition. Relatedly, P2 sets two absolute thresholds (redacted < 2 net, unredacted >= 5 net) on separate conditions rather than a paired test of redacted against unredacted on the same tasks; a 5-vs-2 net-flip gap out of 600 is not distinguishable from noise as a between-condition contrast, so P2 can be 'passed' by a null. P3's 60%-vs-30% divergence-attribution split is asserted with no power calculation over what will be a single- or double-digit set of harmed episodes.
what_would_fix_it: Three changes, in order of importance. (1) Make the k=3 comparison the headline, not a footnote: pre-register 'redacted k=7 beats raw k=3 on clean tasks by at least X net flips' as P0, and drop the study if k=7 has no measurable clean-task advantage over k=3 - that single test decides whether the whole contribution is practically live. (2) Read arXiv:2605.09330 in full and state the three spurious-pattern types before pre-registration, resolving now rather than at write-up whether instance-specific state is already one of them; if it is, re-pitch the paper as the ground-truth census plus the head-to-head clean-cost comparison of controls with CAMEL as a required arm, and say so in the abstract. (3) Fix the statistics: report a paired McNemar of redacted vs unredacted on the identical 600 tasks (not two separate no-memory contrasts), pre-compute the expected discordant-pair count from the pilot and state the minimum detectable coefficient for P1, and if that count is under ~40, abandon the observational regression and rest the causal claim entirely on the redaction/permutation/oracle/length-filler contrast plus the 0/1/2/4/8 controlled dose ladder, which is the part of the design that actually identifies content against volume. Additionally, if the organic bank turns out to be insight-dominated, say in advance what the fallback contribution is rather than letting the study reduce to a controlled-injection design that arXiv:2607.10608 has already run.
missing_baseline: An instruction-only, zero-token-cost epistemic-framing baseline: prepend a fixed caveat that retrieved trajectories describe a different episode whose object placements and container states must be re-verified in the current environment, and leave the facts intact. This is the cheapest possible intervention against the exact mechanism claimed, it costs nothing on clean tasks by construction, and if it matches redaction the paper has no method. The listed 'reliance-steering instruction' is not this - it is a general dial on how much to trust memory (arXiv:2601.05107), not a fact-typed staleness caveat, and the proposal predicts it will trade clean-task loss for safety, which a targeted caveat need not. Secondarily missing: retrieval-side re-ranking on state-fact overlap with the current observation (the agent sees the target room's initial observation before acting, so stale facts are detectable at read time without ground truth), which is the obvious cheap alternative to redaction and is not among the seven controls.
preprint_collision: No verified collision. The proposal's own check is above average for this pipeline - it names each query, its channel, and the returned IDs, it verified three IDs by lookup, and it honestly reports that its WebSearch budget was exhausted and that WebFetch and sandbox arXiv fetches returned nothing - but it is asymmetric: thorough on the diagnosis half (staleness, compliance trap, spurious correlations) and near-empty on the intervention half, since it ran no query at all on the method it proposes (masking, redaction, or placeholder substitution of instance-specific entities in retrieved demonstrations). My searches, all answered by channel (a) the s2cli command over Semantic Scholar + HuggingFace Papers; channel (b) WebSearch was unavailable in this session and WebFetch is blocked, so nothing was answered by (b). Query 1 (mechanism, --recent): 'stale state facts in retrieved agent experience memory ALFWorld negative transfer redaction' returned 2608.04574 (When Memory Lies, spatial staleness in VLM agents), 2607.28272 (MemHarness), 2606.26511 (MemStrata temporal validity, stale-fact errors in RAG over evolving knowledge), 2605.12978 (Useful Memories Become Faulty When Continuously Updated), 2605.06527 (STALE benchmark: can agents know when memories are invalid), 2606.17591, 2606.20529, 2607.12893, 2605.12493, 2601.11653 - staleness of knowledge-base or personalized facts, none labeling an agent's own cross-episode experience facts against environment ground truth. Query 2 (mechanism, unrestricted): 'episode-specific object location facts cause negative transfer in agent experience reuse, fact-level ablation' returned nothing on point (2607.28272, 2607.20972 on situationally-bound operational facts for coding agents, 2607.14514, plus off-topic factuality/interpretability work). Query 3 (closest named method, --recent): 'spurious correlations agentic memory CAMEL calibration write retrieval time clean performance' returned 2605.09330 alone as relevant, confirming the proposal's characterization and confirming CAMEL is the nearest method. Query 4: 'masking or redacting instance-specific entities in retrieved in-context demonstrations to prevent copying wrong details' returned nothing relevant (RedactionBench 2606.18782 and privacy-redaction work only) - so the redaction control appears genuinely unclaimed, which is the proposal's strongest surviving novelty. Query 5 (--recent): 'per-item harm attribution retrieved memory items labeled against environment ground truth leave-one-out agent success flips' returned 2604.05467 (CUE-R, perturbs individual retrieved evidence items and measures correctness change - the closest methodological neighbour to the leave-one-item-out probe, in RAG rather than agents), 2608.00017 (Memory Reward Inflation), nothing on ground-truth fact labeling. Query 6 (--recent): 'stale memory in embodied language agents ALFWorld object placement changes across episodes causes wrong navigation' returned 2608.04574 and 2605.29463 (Honest Lying, ALFWorld) as the two nearest. Query 7 (--recent): 'read-time control abstention utility filtering provenance gating compared head to head agent memory clean task cost' returned 2607.10059 (AgentAbstain), 2606.18829 (GateMem), 2603.15994 (Selective Memory: write-time gating reported to outperform read-time filtering) - no head-to-head of read-time controls on task execution, supporting that gap. Verification: I verified 2605.09330, 2607.10608, 2606.05684, 2604.27003, 2605.05583, 2601.03192, 2608.10509, 2601.05107, 2602.04288, 2605.10828, 2608.04574 and 2605.29463 by direct lookup; every ID the proposal relies on resolved with the claimed date and content. I could not verify 2607.28272, 2608.12847, 2605.30712, 2608.07107, 2605.20926, 2605.23723, 2606.24322 or 2608.30177, which the proposal cites from its own earlier searches; none of them is load-bearing for its novelty argument. Net: the novelty claim survives search, but it survives on the intervention (fact-level redaction at matched tokens with clean-cost accounting), not on the diagnosis, where 2605.09330, 2608.04574 and 2605.29463 already occupy adjacent ground, and where the proposal's differentiator against 2605.09330 remains explicitly unverified by its own authors.
